input.title: Duties to Distrust: The Decentring of Economic and White-collar Crime Policing in Sweden
input.abstract: This article examines a general trend towards the 'decentring' of the policing of economic and white-collar crime in Sweden in recent decades. As a theoretical point of departure, we discuss how the 'decentred policing' concept can link the theoretical approaches of regulation and policing studies. We then analyse five empirical cases in which private actors have been given duties and incentives to report others' crimes, in order to give a detailed account of the expansion and effects of the decentring of business and finance policing. The five cases concern the policing of bankruptcy crimes, money laundering, company management crimes, market abuse and insider dealings, and illegal cartels. The article ends by discussing some possible causes and consequences of this tendency. © 2015 The Author.

output.reasoning: O artigo não atende aos critérios básicos de busca por palavras-chave do protocolo (métodos computacionais, lavagem de dinheiro ou crime organizado) nos campos de título, resumo ou palavras-chave dos autores.
